mainTopic: Benefiting from things brought or done on יום טוב, and whether ראש חודש is mentioned on ראש השנה
overview: The amud opens by finishing אמימר's version of the story about a deer served at the ראש גלותא's house on יום טוב. In this version, the deer had been brought from outside the תחום. רב נחמן and רב חסדא ate from it, because something brought for one Jew is permitted to another Jew. רב ששת did not eat, because anything brought to the ראש גלותא's house is brought with all the רבנן in mind. The גמרא answers the challenge from רב ששת's talk with רבה בר שמואל by saying that, in this version, the talk never happened. Next, רבא permits withered turnips in מחוזא, since they were clearly picked before יום טוב and were brought for non-Jews. He forbids them once the sellers start bringing extra for Jewish buyers. Then רבא rules that myrtle cut on יום טוב שני may not be smelled until one waits בכדי שיעשו, the time it takes to cut it. Finally, the גמרא asks whether ראש חודש must be mentioned separately on ראש השנה. It shows that רבי דוסא's argument with the חכמים is only about saying it with a condition. It then raises a challenge from בית שמאי's count of ten ברכות, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The deer had come from outside the תחום
steps.stepSummary: In אמימר's version, the real issue with the deer was that it was brought from outside the תחום on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it came from outside the תחום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives אמימר's explanation of the deer case: the problem was that it was brought from outside the תחום. This sets up the next two steps, which explain each side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier version said the argument was about the two days of יום טוב, meaning one holiness or two. אמימר moves the whole argument to a different issue: food brought by a non-Jew from beyond the תחום. Now the question becomes who is forbidden to eat such food.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (switches to the correct explanation)
from outside the שבת/יום טוב boundary (2,000 אמה)
it came

phrases.english: Rather, it came from outside the Shabbat limit.
phrases.notes: This is still אמימר's way of telling it: they aren't arguing about two holinesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by continuing אמימר's alternative version of the deer story from the previous daf.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about whether the two days of יום טוב are one holiness or two.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument was about an animal brought from outside the תחום.

steps.title: Why the ones who ate considered it permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב חסדא hold that something brought from outside the תחום for one Jew is permitted to a different Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who ate holds: something brought for this Jew is permitted to another Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב נחמן and רב חסדא ate the deer. In their view, it was brought only for the ראש גלותא, so his guests were allowed to eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on food brought from outside the תחום applies only to the person it was brought for. Since the non-Jew brought the deer for the ראש גלותא, the other רבנן at his table were not the intended recipients and could eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who ate
holds / reasons
what is brought for (the sake of)
another Jew

phrases.english: The one who ate holds:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן and רב חסדא.

phrases.english: something that comes for this Jew
phrases.notes: Brought from outside the תחום on behalf of a specific person.

phrases.english: is permitted to another Jew.
phrases.notes: The ban applies only to the one it was brought for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the argument, based on the new case defined in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food brought from outside the תחום for one Jew is permitted to another Jew.

steps.title: Why the one who did not eat considered it forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת holds that everything brought to the ראש גלותא's house is brought with all the רבנן in mind, so it was forbidden to them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who did not eat holds: whatever comes to the house of the ראש גלותא comes with all the רבנן in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב ששת refused to eat. He held that the guests were also among the people the deer was brought for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת agrees that food brought for one Jew is permitted to another. He argues that this case is different: everyone knew the ראש גלותא hosted the רבנן on יום טוב. So the deer was brought for them as well, and they share the ראש גלותא's prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: and the one who did not eat
the house of the Exilarch
with the intention / in mind of
all the Sages

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת does not reject the rule that food brought for one Jew is permitted to another. He only says that in this house, the guests were part of who it was brought for.

phrases.english: And the one who did not eat holds:
phrases.notes: רב ששת.

phrases.english: anything that comes to the house of the Exilarch
comes with all the Sages in mind.
phrases.notes: So it counts as brought for them too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the argument described in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food brought to the ראש גלותא's house is brought with all the רבנן in mind, so it is forbidden to them as well.
steps.whatToRemember: In אמימר's version, both sides agree on the basic rule. They argue only about whether the guests count as the people the food was brought for.

steps.title: But רב ששת spoke with רבה בר שמואל about it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אמימר's version using the earlier report that רב ששת met רבה בר שמואל and discussed the issue.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב ששת meet רבה בר שמואל and say to him what he said?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אמימר's version of the story. An earlier report has רב ששת meeting רבה בר שמואל and talking about the matter in a way that connects to the two days of יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That conversation suggests that רב ששת's reason was about the holiness of the two days. That does not fit אמימר's claim that the issue was the תחום. The two reports seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: but surely (opens a challenge)
he met him
and said to him

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Sheshet meet
phrases.notes: He means the meeting the גמרא told us about earlier in this סוגיא.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Shmuel and say to him [what he said]?!
phrases.notes: That conversation implied the issue was the two days of יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְרַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the whole version presented in steps 1–3.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's claim that the argument was about the תחום, not the two days of יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reported conversation shows רב ששת was concerned with the two days, which contradicts אמימר's version.

steps.title: That conversation never happened
steps.stepSummary: According to אמימר's version, the meeting with רבה בר שמואל never took place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those things never happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge directly. According to אמימר, the conversation between רב ששת and רבה בר שמואל did not happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of reinterpreting the conversation, the answer denies that it happened at all. The two versions of the story disagree about the facts, so the challenge only works against someone who accepts the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: these things never happened

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the deer story. The first is about the two days of יום טוב. אמימר's is about the תחום. אמימר's version simply denies the רבה בר שמואל conversation.

phrases.english: Those things never happened.
phrases.notes: According to אמימר's version.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denying the factual basis of the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The conversation with רבה בר שמואל proves the issue was the two days of יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to אמימר, that conversation never happened, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: רבא permits buying the turnips in מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: Turnips were brought to מחוזא on יום טוב. רבא saw that they were withered and allowed people to buy them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A shipment of turnips came to מחוזא. רבא went out, saw that they were withered, and permitted buying from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about produce brought on יום טוב. רבא inspects the turnips and allows people to buy them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern was that the turnips might have been picked on יום טוב itself, which would be a forbidden מלאכה. רבא noticed that they were withered, and that physical sign led him to permit them. The next step gives his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: turnip(s)
מחוזא, רבא's town
withered
he permitted
to buy

phrases.english: A certain turnip shipment that came to Mechoza,
phrases.notes: Brought by non-Jewish merchants on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rava went out and saw that it was withered,
phrases.notes: The physical sign he relied on.

phrases.english: and Rava permitted buying from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new case about produce brought on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא permitted buying withered turnips that arrived on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבא's reason: they were picked yesterday
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the withering proves the turnips were picked before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: These were certainly uprooted yesterday.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the reason for his ruling. Withered turnips must have been picked the day before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Freshly picked turnips are not withered, so the turnips' condition proves no forbidden picking happened on יום טוב. רבא uses a visible physical sign to settle a factual doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: certainly
from yesterday
was uprooted / picked

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a clear physical sign can resolve a doubt about whether something was done on יום טוב.

phrases.english: He said: This was certainly uprooted yesterday.
phrases.notes: So no forbidden picking took place on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבא's ruling in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The withered turnips were certainly picked before יום טוב, so buying them was permitted.

steps.title: Coming from outside the תחום is not a problem
steps.stepSummary: רבא heads off a possible objection. He says the turnips are not forbidden for having come from outside the תחום, because they were brought for non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: What might you say, that they came from outside the תחום? Something brought for one Jew may be eaten by another Jew. All the more so these turnips, which were brought with non-Jews in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a second possible problem with the turnips, that they were carried from outside the תחום, and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 רבא settled one issue: the turnips were picked before יום טוב. Now he deals with a different issue, carrying them in from outside the תחום. If something brought for one Jew is allowed for another Jew, then something brought for non-Jews is surely allowed for a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: The boundary (2000 אמה) beyond which one may not walk or carry items in on שבת or יום טוב
What would you say? (introduces a possible objection the speaker will answer)
All the more so (a קל וחומר)
With non-Jews in mind, done for their sake

phrases.english: What would you say,
that they came from outside the Shabbat limit?
Something that was brought for this Jew
is permitted to be eaten by another Jew,
and all the more so this delivery
which came with non-Jews in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's explanation by answering a second possible problem with the turnips.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's permission to buy the turnips
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Things carried in from outside the תחום on יום טוב might be forbidden.
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר from an accepted principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The turnips are forbidden because they crossed the תחום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Items brought for someone else are allowed. Items brought for non-Jews are surely allowed.

steps.title: רבא forbids the turnips once deliveries increase
steps.stepSummary: When רבא saw the sellers bringing larger amounts, clearly aimed at Jewish buyers, he forbade buying them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he saw that they were bringing more and more of them, he forbade them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רבא later changed his ruling because the facts changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission in Step 8 rested on the turnips being brought for non-Jews. Once the extra amounts showed they were being brought for Jews, that reason no longer applied. So רבא forbade them.

keyTerms.meaning: They increase, bring more
He forbade

steps.whatToRemember: A היתר based on 'it was done for non-Jews' ends once it is clear the item is being brought for Jews.

phrases.english: Once he saw
that they were bringing increased amounts of them
he forbade them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזָא דְּקָא מַפְּשִׁי וּמַיְיתִי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission of Step 8 once its reason no longer holds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the turnips are evidently brought for Jews, buying them is forbidden.

steps.title: רבינא allows smelling myrtle cut on the second day of יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: Canopy makers cut myrtle on יום טוב שני. That evening רבינא allowed people to smell it immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some canopy makers cut myrtle for themselves on the second day of יום טוב. In the evening רבינא allowed them to smell it right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about benefiting from work done on יום טוב, here the second day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting a plant is forbidden on יום טוב. יום טוב שני, however, is only a rabbinic custom in the diaspora. So רבינא did not require waiting after יום טוב before enjoying the myrtle's smell.

keyTerms.meaning: Canopy makers, who wove myrtle into canopies
Myrtle
The second day of יום טוב kept outside ארץ ישראל
Immediately

phrases.english: Certain canopy makers
who cut myrtle for themselves
on the second day of a Festival,
in the evening Ravina permitted them
to smell it immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ בְּנֵי גְנָנָא דְּגַזּוּ לְהוּ אָסָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case on the same theme of benefiting from things done on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Myrtle cut on יום טוב שני may be smelled immediately that night.

steps.title: רבא בר תחליפא urges forbidding it because the workers are not learned
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר תחליפא tells רבינא to forbid it, since these workers are not learned. They might come to treat יום טוב שני lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר תחליפא said to רבינא: The Master should forbid it to them, because they are not learned in Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא pushes back on רבינא's leniency and asks for a stricter ruling for these people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not reject רבינא's reasoning in general. He argues that unlearned people need a stricter rule so they keep respecting the second day.

keyTerms.meaning: People learned in Torah
Let the Master forbid it to them

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rava bar Taḥalifa said to Ravina:
Let the Master forbid it to them
because they are not learned in Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא לְרָבִינָא: לֵיסַר לְהוּ מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's leniency for this particular group.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's permission to smell the myrtle immediately
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unlearned people may come to treat יום טוב שני lightly, so the rabbis should be strict with them.

steps.title: רב שמעיה says even learned people must wait
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה objects that the issue has nothing to do with being learned. Everyone must wait the time it takes to cut the myrtle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה objected: The reason is that they are not learned. Does that mean learned people would be allowed? But we require waiting the time it takes to do the work!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיה attacks the reason רבא בר תחליפא gave. He says there is a basic requirement to wait that applies to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא בר תחליפא's wording implies that learned people could smell the myrtle immediately. רב שמעיה says that is wrong. After a forbidden act on יום טוב, everyone must wait בכדי שיעשו, the time the work would take, so that no one gains from the forbidden work.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it
Implying that (draws an inference from the wording)
The amount of time it takes to do the work

steps.confusionAlert: רב שמעיה is not being more lenient. He is saying the prohibition is broader: it applies to learned people too, not just unlearned ones.

phrases.english: Rav Shemaya strongly objects to this:
The reason is that they are not learned in Torah;
so if they were learned in Torah, it would be permitted?!
But we require waiting the time needed to do it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in Step 11 and, along with it, רבינא's leniency.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא בר תחליפא's reason, and by extension רבינא's permission
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reason implies learned people may smell the myrtle immediately, but everyone must wait בכדי שיעשו.

steps.title: רבא rules that one must wait the time it takes to do the work
steps.stepSummary: They asked רבא, and he ruled that one must wait בכדי שיעשו.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went and asked רבא. He told them: We require waiting the time it takes to do the work.
steps.whatsHappening: The question goes to רבא, who decides the matter in line with רב שמעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling settles the debate. Even after יום טוב שני, a person may not benefit right away from forbidden work done that day. One must wait as long as the work itself would take.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him
We require

steps.whatToRemember: After forbidden work on יום טוב, even on יום טוב שני, one must wait בכדי שיעשו before benefiting. This applies to everyone, learned or not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rabbis treat יום טוב שני seriously, applying the same waiting rule as they do elsewhere.

phrases.english: They went and asked Rava,
he said to them: We require waiting the time needed to do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute in favor of רב שמעיה's position.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One must wait בכדי שיעשו after יום טוב שני before smelling myrtle cut that day.

steps.title: Returning to רבי דוסא's words in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of רבי דוסא's opinion in the משנה, to start a new discussion about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: The one who leads the prayers before the ark, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the משנה as a heading. This sets up the next discussion, which will use רבי דוסא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי דוסא says the חזן on ראש השנה asks, "Strengthen us on this day of ראש חודש, whether it is today or tomorrow." The חכמים did not agree with him. Those details matter for the coming steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who passes before the ark, meaning the חזן leading the תפילה
"etc.": the quote continues as it appears in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says:
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: The one who passes before the ark, etc.
phrases.notes: He says: "on this day of the New Moon, whether today or tomorrow."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of יום טוב שני and the myrtle, and returns to a new line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסא: the חזן mentions ראש חודש on ראש השנה with a condition (today or tomorrow).

steps.title: Must ראש חודש be mentioned separately on ראש השנה?
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports a question from רב הונא's study hall: does one mention ראש חודש in the תפילה of ראש השנה? The question has two sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: When we were in the house of רב הונא, we asked: Must one mention ראש חודש on ראש השנה? Since the two days have different מוסף offerings, do we mention it separately? Or perhaps one זכרון counts for both?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks whether the תפילה of ראש השנה must also mention ראש חודש. ראש השנה always falls on ראש חודש of תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: ראש חודש and ראש השנה each have their own מוסף offering, so perhaps each needs its own mention. Side two: both days are called a day of זכרון (remembrance), so mentioning זכרון once may cover both.

keyTerms.meaning: We had a question; a real halachic doubt
To mention in the תפילה
The additional offerings brought on special days
Remembrance; a name used for both ראש השנה and ראש חודש
Or perhaps; introduces the other side of a question

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the question is whether ראש השנה is a real יום טוב. It is about whether the ראש חודש side of the day needs its own mention, or whether the one זכרון covers it.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
When we were in the house of Rav Huna,
phrases.notes: In his בית מדרש.

phrases.english: we had a question:
What is the law about mentioning Rosh Chodesh
on Rosh Hashana?
Since they are separate in their Mussaf offerings,
phrases.notes: Each day has its own מוסף.

phrases.english: do we say (mention) it?
Or perhaps:
one 'remembrance' counts for this and for that?
phrases.notes: Mentioning יום הזכרון covers both.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לַן: מַהוּ לְהַזְכִּיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the question that רבי דוסא's opinion (step 14) will be used to answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ראש חודש must be mentioned separately in the תפילה of ראש השנה, or whether one זכרון covers both.

steps.title: רב הונא tries to answer from רבי דוסא's dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the answer is already in the משנה: the חכמים disagree with רבי דוסא, so they must hold that ראש חודש is not mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to us: You learned it already. רבי דוסא says: The one who leads the prayers, etc. Isn't the argument about whether to mention ראש חודש?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings proof from the משנה. רבי דוסא mentions ראש חודש, and the חכמים argue with him, so their argument must be about mentioning it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא reads the dispute this way: רבי דוסא says to mention ראש חודש, and the חכמים say not to. That would mean one זכרון is enough, the second side of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: You have already learned it (in a משנה or ברייתא)
Is it not that...? Introduces a suggested proof

phrases.english: He (Rav Huna) said to us:
You have learned it:
Rabbi Dosa says:
The one who passes before the ark, etc.,
phrases.notes: And the חכמים did not agree with him.

phrases.english: Is it not about mentioning (Rosh Chodesh)?
phrases.notes: So the חכמים would hold that it is not mentioned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 using the משנה quoted in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That ראש חודש is not mentioned separately on ראש השנה (according to the חכמים), because one זכרון covers both.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רבי דוסא and the חכמים in the משנה.

steps.title: The dispute is about the condition, not the mention
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the חכמים may disagree only about saying it with a condition, "today or tomorrow."
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the argument is about making a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב הונא's proof. The argument may only be about the תנאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא's new point may be the condition ("whether today or tomorrow"), added because the date is uncertain. The חכמים may reject only that condition, while everyone might agree that ראש חודש is mentioned. So the משנה does not settle רבה's question.

keyTerms.meaning: To make a condition, i.e., to say "whether today or tomorrow"
A condition

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's question stays open here. Separate מוספין point toward a separate mention, and one זכרון points toward one mention. The משנה cannot decide it, because the argument there may be only about the תנאי.

phrases.english: No, it is about making a condition.
phrases.notes: The dispute is about "today or tomorrow," not about mentioning ראש חודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not decide the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the dispute was about mentioning ראש חודש. It may be only about adding the condition.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the idea that the argument is about the condition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the דחיה: רבי דוסא used his conditional wording on every doubtful ראש חודש of the year, and the חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This reading also makes sense, because a ברייתא teaches: רבי דוסא did the same thing on the ראשי חדשים of the whole year, and the חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now supports the answer from Step 17 by quoting a ברייתא. The next step will explain exactly why this ברייתא is a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the חכמים might only reject the condition "today or tomorrow." Now the גמרא adds a new fact: the same argument also happened on regular ראשי חדשים. This fact will show that the argument cannot be about mentioning ראש חודש at all.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical. This phrase introduces support for what was just said.
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה
The first days of the months
They did not agree with him

phrases.english: So too, it is reasonable,
since it is taught in a baraita:
And so too Rabbi Dosa would do
phrases.notes: He used the wording "today or tomorrow".

phrases.aramaic: בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים שֶׁל כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ,
phrases.english: on the New Moons of the entire year,
phrases.notes: These are the months where there is a doubt about which day is ראש חודש.

phrases.english: and they did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the דחיה of Step 17 with an outside source.
steps.raayaObject: The argument between רבי דוסא and the חכמים is about saying ראש חודש with a condition, not about mentioning ראש חודש at all.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying that רבי דוסא did the same on all doubtful ראשי חדשים and the חכמים disagreed.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא proves that the argument is about the condition
steps.stepSummary: If the argument is about the condition, it makes sense that the חכמים disagreed on regular ראשי חדשים too. If it were about mentioning ראש חודש, why would they disagree? Everyone mentions ראש חודש on ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works fine if you say the argument is about making a condition: that is why they did not agree with him. But if you say the argument is about mentioning ראש חודש, why did they not agree with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the logic of the proof from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular ראש חודש, nobody would say you should leave out the mention of ראש חודש. So when the חכמים disagree there, the only possible point of argument is the condition "today or tomorrow." This also shows that רב הונא's proof in Step 16 does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out fine. One side makes sense, and the other side is about to be challenged.
To make a condition, by saying "today or tomorrow"
To mention ראש חודש in the תפילה
Why?

phrases.english: Granted, if you say the argument is about making a condition,
that is why they did not agree with him.
But if you say the argument is about mentioning ראש חודש at all,
why did they not agree with him?
phrases.notes: On a regular ראש חודש, mentioning it is obviously correct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 18 with a בשלמא argument.
steps.raayaObject: The argument is about the condition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The disagreement on regular ראשי חדשים, which can only be about the condition.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי דוסא and the חכמים is about saying "today or tomorrow" as a condition, not about whether to mention ראש חודש.

steps.title: Why argue about the condition in two separate cases?
steps.stepSummary: If the argument is only about the condition, it is the same question on ראש השנה and on any ראש חודש. So why teach the argument in both cases?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what, the argument is about the condition? Why do I need them to argue in two cases?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the argument is about the condition, but now asks why it had to be taught twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches the argument for ראש השנה, and the ברייתא teaches it for all other ראשי חדשים. If the issue is the same condition each time, one case should have been enough. This is a challenge about repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: But then what? This introduces a problem with the view just accepted.
Why do I need it?
For them to argue in two cases

phrases.english: But rather, what? The argument is about making a condition?
Why do I need them to argue in two cases?
phrases.notes: The two cases are ראש השנה and the other ראשי חדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מַאי לְהַתְנוֹת? לְמָה לִי לְאִיפְּלוֹגֵי בְּתַרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 19 by pointing out an apparent repetition.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the argument is only about the condition, which seems to make the second case extra.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the issue is the same in both cases, teaching the argument twice adds nothing.

steps.title: Why teaching only ראש השנה would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If we knew only the ראש השנה case, we might think the חכמים object there only because people could treat the יום טוב lightly. Then we might think they agree with רבי דוסא on a regular ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. If we had been taught only ראש השנה, I would have said: here the חכמים say no, because people might come to treat the day lightly. But on the ראשי חדשים of the rest of the year, I would say they agree with רבי דוסא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a צריכא: both cases were needed. Here it explains the first half: why the ראש השנה case alone would not teach us enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ראש השנה, saying "today or tomorrow" could make people think the day's holiness is only a doubt, so they might treat it lightly and even do forbidden work. A regular ראש חודש has no ban on work, so that worry does not exist there. Without the second case, we could have thought the חכמים agree with רבי דוסא on a regular ראש חודש.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed. Both teachings are necessary.
I would have thought. This is the mistaken first idea.
To treat lightly, to disrespect
I might say

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves of the צריכא. This half explains what we might wrongly think about the חכמים. The next half explains what we might wrongly think about רבי דוסא.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
because if it had taught us only Rosh HaShana,
I would have said:
in this case the Rabbis say no,
because people will come to treat it lightly,
phrases.notes: People might treat the יום טוב as only a doubt and do forbidden work.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים שֶׁל כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ —
phrases.english: but on the New Moons of the entire year,
I might say they agree with Rabbi Dosa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20 by showing why the second case is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something the other case could not teach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only ראש השנה, we would think the חכמים object only because of the worry about treating the day lightly, and that they agree with רבי דוסא on a regular ראש חודש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא about regular ראשי חדשים shows that the חכמים reject the condition even there.

steps.title: Why teaching only the regular ראש חודש would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If we knew only the regular ראש חודש case, we might think רבי דוסא allows the condition only there. Then we might think he agrees with the חכמים on ראש השנה. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had been said only in this case, I would say that only here רבי דוסא says it, but in that case I would say he agrees with the חכמים. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא with the second half and closes by repeating "it is needed."
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular ראש חודש there is no worry about people treating it lightly, so רבי דוסא's condition is easy to accept. On ראש השנה that worry exists, so we might have thought רבי דוסא would agree with the חכמים there. The ראש השנה case in the משנה shows that רבי דוסא holds his view even there.

keyTerms.meaning: In this case. Here it means a regular ראש חודש.
In that other case. Here it means ראש השנה.
He agrees

steps.whatToRemember: The argument about the condition is taught in two cases. Each case shows that one side holds its view even where we might have thought it would give in: the חכמים on a regular ראש חודש, and רבי דוסא on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: And if it had been stated only in this case,
phrases.notes: This refers to a regular ראש חודש.

phrases.english: I would say that in this case Rabbi Dosa says it,
but in that other case,
phrases.notes: This refers to ראש השנה.

phrases.english: I might say he agrees with the Rabbis.
It is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכא begun in Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the regular ראש חודש case, we would think רבי דוסא agrees with the חכמים on ראש השנה because of the worry about treating the day lightly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה about ראש השנה shows that רבי דוסא allows the condition even there.

steps.title: A ברייתא about ראש השנה that falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a ברייתא: when ראש השנה is on שבת, בית שמאי say to daven ten ברכות and בית הלל say nine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא objects from a ברייתא: When ראש השנה falls on שבת, בית שמאי say a person davens ten ברכות, and בית הלל say a person davens nine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a source to set up a challenge that comes in the next line. Here it only reports a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about how many ברכות are in the עמידה when ראש השנה is on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ראש השנה עמידה (מוסף) normally has nine ברכות. בית שמאי add a tenth ברכה just for שבת, so each special day gets its own ברכה. בית הלל put שבת inside the ברכה of the day, so it stays nine.

keyTerms.meaning: That happened to fall on שבת
The school of שמאי
The school of הלל
He davens (says the עמידה)

steps.confusionAlert: The ten and the nine are not two different ways of counting the same תפילה. They are a real מחלוקת about whether שבת gets its own separate ברכה. בית שמאי give it one (ten in total). בית הלל fold it into another ברכה (nine in total).

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rosh HaShana
phrases.notes: מיתיבי signals that a source is being brought to challenge something.

phrases.english: that happened to fall on Shabbat,
Beit Shammai say: one prays ten [blessings],
phrases.notes: The nine of ראש השנה plus a separate ברכה for שבת.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: one prays nine.
phrases.notes: שבת is mentioned inside the ברכה of the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of the condition, the גמרא brings a new source to test the idea that ראש חודש must be mentioned separately on ראש השנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When ראש השנה is on שבת: בית שמאי say ten ברכות (a separate one for שבת), and בית הלל say nine.

steps.title: Then בית שמאי should require eleven
steps.stepSummary: If ראש חודש needed its own mention on ראש השנה, בית שמאי, who give each special day its own ברכה, should have said eleven ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were true that ראש חודש must be mentioned separately, בית שמאי should have said eleven ברכות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to attack the idea that ראש חודש must get its own separate mention in the ראש השנה תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי's method is one ברכה for each special day: nine for ראש השנה and one more for שבת. ראש השנה is also ראש חודש. So if ראש חודש had to be mentioned separately, בית שמאי should count one more ברכה for it, making eleven. Since they say only ten, it seems ראש חודש is not mentioned separately on ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it were so (if that view really existed)
Eleven
It should have been, he should have needed

steps.whyThisMatters: This puts pressure on any view that requires a separate mention of ראש חודש on ראש השנה. The גמרא will need to explain why ראש חודש might not count as its own ברכה even for בית שמאי.

phrases.english: And if it were so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if there really were a view that ראש חודש is mentioned separately on ראש השנה.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: Beit Shammai should have required eleven!
phrases.notes: Nine for ראש השנה, one for שבת, and one for ראש חודש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that ראש חודש must be mentioned separately in the ראש השנה תפילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית שמאי give each special day its own ברכה, which is why they say ten when ראש השנה falls on שבת. If ראש חודש also needed a separate mention, the total would be eleven. The ברייתא says ten, so ראש חודש seems not to be mentioned separately.
